The Program

How the program fits together

The School Teaches

How This Curriculum Works

Four phases, in the manual's build order

The 14 lessons run in four phases and follow the Assembly Manual's build order exactly — the class never builds ahead of the manual, and the manual never asks for a part the box has not reached yet. Lessons 1–7 build the robot, Lessons 8–9 bring it to life, Lessons 10–11 drive it and record it, and Lessons 12–14 teach it to perform a task on its own.

Every lesson, the same shape

Each lesson lists the same six elements, in the same order:

GoalThe one outcome the lesson exists to produce, stated before anyone picks up a tool.
What gets built / doneThe concrete work of the session, in the manual's build order.
Session flowOpen (5 min) — recap and today's goal. Build — the hands-on work. Check — the class verifies the work against the checkoff before anyone packs up.
Key skillsWhat students are actually practising, so progress can be described to parents and administrators in plain words.
Done looks likeThe checkoff: observable, gradeable evidence that the lesson landed. No checkoff, no moving on.
Teacher notesWhat to prep before class, and the one stuck point to watch for while students work.

The kit teaches the order

The kit's trays are packed in build order, so the parts a lesson needs are the parts on top. A team lays out only the current tray zone, builds, and checks off — the box itself enforces the sequence and keeps small parts from wandering.

MAKER classes print ahead

In the MAKER edition, each stage's printed parts are printed before the lesson that builds them — the print queue runs one stage ahead of the lessons, so printing never holds a class up. COMPLETE classes skip the queue and start at the tray.

One rule runs through all 14 lessons: a stage is finished only when its checkoff passes. A team that finishes early helps another team or practises in the simulator — nobody builds ahead on unverified work.

Pacing at a Glance

One program, two paces

The same 14 lessons, run at the pace the school's timetable allows. The phases land in the same order on both lanes — only the weeks change.

COURSES
The 14 lessons, step by step — tap a lesson to open it

Every lesson follows the Assembly Manual's build order exactly. Open a lesson to see its complete dossier — goal, the full step-by-step in order, key skills, teacher notes, and the checkoff that closes it. The full Assembly Manual is one tap away, top right.

Program Requirement · Read before Lesson 1
Applies Every session, Lessons 1–14 | Posted in the room

Sourccey is a real machine — about a metre tall, with powered arms, a lift, and a lithium battery. These five rules are not suggestions. The teacher states them in Lesson 1, posts them in the room, and enforces them in every session that follows.

1 · Soldering is teacher-led

One step in the whole build uses a soldering iron: the potentiometer wires, in Lesson 7. It is done teacher-led, with gloves and ventilation, exactly as the Assembly Manual shows. Students prepare, hold, and inspect; the teacher runs the iron. No other lesson involves soldering, and the iron is never left unattended or passed hand to hand.

2 · Battery discipline

The robot runs on a LiFePO4 battery pack. Charge it only with the chargers included in the kit — never a substitute charger. At every power-up, check the battery gauge before doing anything else, and say the reading out loud so the whole team hears it. A pack that is swollen, punctured, hot, or reading abnormally comes out of service and goes to the teacher immediately.

3 · No adhesives on structural joints

If a joint does not fit, the fix is mechanical: unbolt it and refit it. Glue and tape on a structural joint hide a misalignment, make the next stage harder, and turn a five-minute refit into a broken part. Adhesives stay out of the build unless the manual itself calls for them.

4 · Two-person lift, power off

Built, Sourccey weighs 15.88 kg. Moving it is always a two-person lift, and the robot is powered off before it is moved every time, even across the room. Lift from the base, never by the arms, dome, or lift.

5 · Driving sessions are supervised

Driving Sourccey (Lesson 10) is always supervised: one driver at a time, a cleared drive area, and the robot's off switch within the teacher's reach.

CARE OF THE MACHINE
Power off before hands-on work

Any time hands go inside the body — wiring, refits, inspection — the robot is off first.

Know the off switch

From Lesson 9 onward, every student must be able to find and use the power-off switch without looking it up. The teacher checks this; it is part of the Lesson 9 checkoff.

Servos are not hand-cranks

Outside the hand tests the lessons specify, joints are moved by the controls, not forced by hand.

Epoxy work follows the manual's PPE

The wheel housings (Lesson 1, Manual Stage 0) are bonded with structural epoxy. While it is uncured it releases fumes: nitrile gloves, a face mask rated for organic fumes, and a well-ventilated area, exactly as the manual's safety note requires — and the bonded housings cure for at least an hour before they carry any load.

End every session tidy

Parts back in their tray zone, cables as the manual routes them, build log updated. The next session starts from a known state.

7 lessonsManual Stages 0–11, in build order

Seven lessons take the robot from a box of parts to a wired machine with two arms, a lift, and a head. Nothing is powered yet — Phase 1 is mechanical craft: fit, alignment, and checking work against the manual.

Assembly Manual · Stage 0 prep + Stage 4 base
Pacing Lane A · Week 1 | Lane B · Week 1 — paired with Lesson 2
GOALTour the finished robot and the box; assemble the base plates and mecanum wheels.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You start by touring the finished robot and the box, then assemble the base plates and mecanum wheels that everything else stands on.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open — the destination moment (5 min)
    Before anyone builds, the teacher runs the finished robot through its task while the class watches: this is where the course leads — the machine they will build and then teach. Then meet the robot: what it is, and what the class will build and teach it.
  2. 2
    Unbox and inventory · Stage 0 prep
    Trays out in build order; every part verified against the packing map checklist before any tools come out. A part that is missing is found now, not in Lesson 7.
  3. 3
    Build the four wheel housings · Stage 0 — wheel housings
    Fasten each Wheel Motor into its Wheel Holder — (6) M3x5mm per housing. The holders are handed: FL & RR pair, FR & RL pair. The mecanum wheels look identical at first glance but are not — match each wheel to its holder against Figure 0.8, with the rollers oriented as the figure shows.
  4. 4
    Bond and fit the wheels — teacher-supervised epoxy · Stage 0 — wheel housings
    Apply epoxy to the wheel motor shaft, fasten the wheel coupler with the set screw (the shorter of the two screws in the wheel kit), apply epoxy to the coupler's outer surface, then fasten the mecanum wheel with the center screw (the longer screw). Repeat for all four housings, then leave the epoxy to cure at least 1 hour before the housings are loaded. Epoxy safety per the manual: nitrile gloves, a face mask rated for organic fumes, and a well-ventilated area while it is uncured.
  5. 5
    Assemble the base plates and rear wall · Stage 4 — base
    Fasten the wheel housing assemblies to the Level 1 Base Plates — (44) M3x16mm — and fasten the Linear Actuator Base to the plates — (8) M3x8mm. Thread all wheel motor wires through as you go. Then fasten the Battery Holder to the rear base plate — (4) M3x12mm — and the Level 1 Rear Wall to it — (4) M3x16mm.
  6. 6
    Check
    Inventory signed off against the packing map; roll test and parts-naming round against the checkoff.
KEY SKILLS
Parts identificationReading a photo guideFastener basics
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: finished robot ready to perform its task for the destination moment; a packing map checklist per team; base tray zone laid out per team. Watch for: mecanum wheels fitted in the wrong orientation — the roller pattern must match the manual's photo, or the base will not roll true in every direction.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Every part verified against the packing map checklist; base rolls freely in every direction; every wheel spins true; team can name 10 parts.
Assembly Manual · Stages 6–8
Pacing Lane A · Week 2 | Lane B · Week 1 — paired with Lesson 1
GOALStack and fasten the body walls and levels onto the base.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You stack and fasten the body walls and levels onto the base, keeping each level square and flush as you go.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    Recap the roll test; today's goal — three levels, square and flush.
  2. 2
    First level — front wall, sensors, walls · Stage 6
    Fasten the LiDAR Sensor and Camera to the 1st Level Front Wall — (4) M2.5x5mm, (3) M3x8mm — and mount the IMU on its bracket. Fasten the 1st level walls (the Stage 0 door and hinge-wall assemblies among them) to the base plates — (12) M3x16mm. Set the three 2nd Level Base Plates on top — (6) M3x12mm — with the four Plate Connectors — (8) M3x12mm, (8) M3 Nut — and fit the four Side Flares.
  3. 3
    Second level — walls, drivers, the Pi · Stage 7
    Fasten the 2nd Level Walls to the base plates — (8) M3x25mm, (8) M3 Nut — then the 3rd Level Base Plates to the walls, the same way. Fit the two Circle Accessory Bases. Mount the two Motor Driver Boards on their holders to the 3rd Level Base Plates — (8) M3x12mm for the holders, (8) M2.5x8mm for the boards — and connect their barrel-jack power cables. Fasten the Potentiometer Assembly to the 3rd Level Front Base Plate — (4) M3x20mm — and plug its wire into the PCB, threaded between the two arm braces. Fit the Anti-Deflection Shaft, then fasten the Raspberry Pi Assembly to the 3rd Level Rear Base Plate — (4) M3x12mm — and connect its GPIO Ribbon Cable to the PCB.
  4. 4
    Third level — speakers, handles, dome plates · Stage 8
    Prepare the 3rd Level Front Wall: the three Rectangle Designs and the Breastplate — (8) M3x8mm. Install the speakers on the 3rd Level Walls — (8) M3x12mm, (8) M3 Washers — and plug them into the Raspberry Pi Assembly. Fasten the walls to the 3rd Level Base Plates — (8) M3x25mm, (8) M3 Nut. Fit a Carry Handle and Circle Accessory Base on each side wall, then the Dome Level Base Plates on top of the walls, and the Anti-Deflection Shaft through to the dome level.
  5. 5
    Check
    Squareness and panel fit inspected against the manual before fasteners are final-tightened.
KEY SKILLS
AlignmentSequencingChecking work against the manual
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: body tray zones out; a square or straight edge per team helps the check. Watch for: forced fasteners — a screw that needs force means a panel is misaligned. The lesson's rule applies: unbolt and refit, never force.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Three levels stacked square, panels flush, no forced fasteners.
Assembly Manual · Stage 9
Pacing Lane A · Week 3 | Lane B · Week 2 — paired with Lesson 4
GOALAssemble the linear actuator and mount it in the body.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You assemble the linear actuator — the mechanism behind the lift's up-and-down travel — and mount it in the body.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    What linear motion is — straight-line travel, up and down — and where the lift sits in the body.
  2. 2
    Build the actuator core · Stage 9
    Fasten the Core Upper, Core Lower, and Connectors together — (32) M3x8mm. This is the spine of the lift; keep it flat on the bench and check it stays true as the fasteners go in.
  3. 3
    Build the rack and fit it to the core · Stage 9
    Fasten Rack Upper to Rack Lower — (2) M3x20mm — then fasten the rack to the Linear Actuator Core — (4) M3x20mm. Teeth meshed cleanly along the whole joint, no rocking.
  4. 4
    Fit the arms, braces, and grommet strips · Stage 9
    Fasten the Top Brace, Hypotenuse Brace, and Grommet Strip to each actuator arm — (2) M3x20mm each — then fasten the arms to the core — (6) M3x10mm each. Grommet strips sit with the flat side oriented outwards, as the manual specifies.
  5. 5
    Seat the actuator in the body and pin it · Stage 9
    Insert the actuator assembly into the Anti-Deflection Shaft with the actuator fully extended, so it fits into the hole at the top of the core — if it will not seat, the extension is the first thing to check. Fasten the core with the Linear Actuator Pin: a tight fit, and the manual recommends a small mallet. Fasten the grommet strips to the 2nd Level Walls, then feed the Arm Motor Cable and Camera Cable through the channel in the Top Brace, both sides.
  6. 6
    Check
    Hand-crank test through the full stroke, watching for binding or wobble.
KEY SKILLS
How linear motion worksMechanical patience
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: actuator parts laid out; the 402 mm actuator is the longest part in the kit — clear bench space for it. Watch for: rushing the stroke test. A lift that binds at one point in its travel gets unbolted and refit now, not discovered in Lesson 9.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Lift travels its full stroke smoothly by hand-crank test; the 402 mm actuator seated and braced.
Assembly Manual · Stage 10
Pacing Lane A · Week 4 | Lane B · Week 2 — paired with Lesson 3
GOALMotor supports, bicep, forearm, wrist, gripper for the first arm.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You build the first arm section by section — motor supports, bicep, forearm, wrist, and gripper — handling the servos carefully as each joint goes together.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    Degrees of freedom — count the joints on a human arm, then find the robot's five. Before any motor is touched, the manual's horn rule: every servo carries two horns — the Driven Motor Horn has teeth on the inside, the Idle Motor Horn does not — and both go on before installation unless a step says otherwise. Two motors are the exceptions, and the steps below flag them.
  2. 2
    Shoulder and bicep · Stage 10
    Insert Motor 1 into the Arm Base. Fasten the Planets to the Shoulder — (4) M3x20mm, (4) Planet Bearings — then the Shoulder to Motor 1 — (8) M3x8mm — and the Motor 1 Support to the Arm Base. Insert Motor 2 into the Shoulder — do NOT attach the Driven Motor Horn to Motor 2 — fit the Motor 2 Support, then the Sun Gear with its Driven Motor Horn to Motor 2. Fasten the Bicep to Motor 2 — (4) M3x14mm — and the Bicep Ring Gear across Bicep and Shoulder — (6) M3x25mm.
  3. 3
    Forearm and wrist · Stage 10
    Fasten Motor 3 and its support to the Bicep, then the Forearm to Motor 3 — (8) M3x14mm. Fasten Motor 4 and its support to the Forearm. Fasten Motor 5 and its support to the Wrist — do NOT attach the Driven Motor Horn to Motor 5 — then the Wrist to Motor 4 — (8) M3x8mm.
  4. 4
    Gripper · Stage 10
    Fasten the Driven Motor Horn to the Gripper Base — gripper bases are left/right specific; confirm the correct one before the fasteners go in — then the Gripper Base Assembly to Motor 5. Insert Motor 6 into the Gripper Base, fasten the Gripper Finger to Motor 6 — (8) M3x12mm — and the Motor 6 Support to the base.
  5. 5
    Wire the arm, then mount it · Stage 10
    Connect the motor wire chain and clip each run as it is laid: 170mm from Motor 5 to Motor 6, 100mm from Motor 5 to Motor 4, 200mm from Motor 4 to Motor 3, 200mm from Motor 3 to Motor 2, 120mm from Motor 2 to Motor 1, each with its wire clip. Fasten the Arm Base to the end of the Linear Actuator Arm — (4) M3x16mm, taking care not to overtighten — connect the 400mm Arm Motor Wire to Motor 1, thread the Camera Cable through the arm channels, and fasten the Camera and Arm Camera Cover to the Gripper Base.
  6. 6
    Check
    Move the arm through all 5 DOF by hand; open and close the gripper.
KEY SKILLS
Servo handlingJoint assemblyDegrees of freedom
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: time each team — Lesson 5 is a race against this lesson's time. Watch for: servos handled by their shafts or forced into horns. Servos are fitted, never forced; a joint that binds gets refit, not pushed through.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Arm moves through all 5 DOF by hand without binding; gripper opens and closes.
Assembly Manual · Stage 10
Pacing Lane A · Week 5 | Lane B · Week 3 — paired with Lesson 6
GOALRepeat the arm build from memory, faster and cleaner.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You repeat the arm build for the second arm — this time from memory, faster and cleaner, verifying it against the first arm as your reference.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    Lesson 4 times on the board; team roles assigned — builder, parts runner, checker.
  2. 2
    Build the second arm from memory · Stage 10
    Second arm, manual closed at first; teams open it only to verify. The build order is Lesson 4's exactly — shoulder and bicep, forearm and wrist, gripper, then the wire chain (170 / 100 / 200 / 200 / 120mm) and the camera. Two manual details carry over and are checked, not remembered loosely: no Driven Motor Horn on Motors 2 and 5, and the gripper base and Motor 6 parts for this side are the opposite hand from arm one.
  3. 3
    Check
    Verify against arm one — a mirror and mechanical comparison, joint by joint and gripper to gripper, signed off as its own checkoff — and the clock.
KEY SKILLS
Mastery through repetitionTeam rolesVerification against a reference
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: Lesson 4 times recorded; arm one kept visible as the reference. Watch for: speed beating care. The checkoff demands both — faster and fewer manual checks, with the same no-binding standard as Lesson 4.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Second arm matches the first, with the mirror / mechanical comparison checkoff passed joint by joint; team beat their Lesson 4 time with fewer manual checks.
Assembly Manual · Stage 11
Pacing Lane A · Week 6 | Lane B · Week 3 — paired with Lesson 5
GOALAssemble the dome: eye platform, camera holder, head shell.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You assemble the head — the dome's eye platform and camera holder first, then the head shell closes over them.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    The dome is the robot's face — cameras are its eyes, and placement decides what it can see.
  2. 2
    Seat the two cameras · Stage 11
    Fasten the two Cameras to the Camera Holder on the side marked 'Cameras' — (8) M2.5x8mm — then fasten the Camera Holder Assembly to the Eye Camera Housing — (3) M3x8mm. Both cameras square in the housing before anything closes over them.
  3. 3
    Close the dome shell · Stage 11
    Fasten the Eye Camera Housing Assembly to the Dome Front — (2) M3x20mm. Fasten Dome Front, Dome Left, Dome Right, and Dome Rear to the Dome Top — (12) M3x10mm — then the Magnet Cap and Magnet to the Dome Top — (4) M3x12mm.
  4. 4
    Mount the dome and fit the screen · Stage 11
    Fasten the Dome Assembly to the Dome Level Base Plates — (12) M3x8mm — and the Grommet Strip Covers over the grommet strips. Fasten the LCD Screen to its holder — (4) M3x12mm — then the holder assembly to the Dome Rear — (2) M3x10mm, (2) M3x40mm.
  5. 5
    Check
    Dome closed and opened again cleanly; cameras seated; LCD pocket test-fitted.
KEY SKILLS
Fitting printed partsCamera placement
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: dome parts out; handle printed shells by their edges. Watch for: cameras seated at an angle in the faceplate. A tilted camera means a tilted view in every recording the class ever makes — reseat it now.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Dome closes cleanly; cameras seated in the faceplate; LCD pocket fitted.
Assembly Manual · Stage 5 + Stages 1–3 (teleoperator + motor IDs)
Pacing Lane A · Week 7 | Lane B · Week 4 — paired with Lesson 8
GOALInstall battery, PCB, Raspberry Pi 5, motor drivers, LiDAR, touchscreen; build the Teleoperator leader arms.
MU EXPLAINS IT
You install the electronics — battery, PCB, Raspberry Pi 5, motor drivers, LiDAR, and touchscreen — routing the wiring as the manual shows, then build the Teleoperator leader arms.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    The system map — power, brain, drivers, senses — drawn once, referred to all session. Safety rules restated: power stays off, and the soldering step is teacher-led.
  2. 2
    The Stage 0 sub-assemblies this lesson needs · Stage 0 prep
    Two Stage 0 sub-assemblies land here. The Raspberry Pi Assembly: standoffs on the Pi 5, the USB HAT on the standoffs, the GPIO Ribbon Cable connected to the HAT, the Power Board fastened on, HAT linked to Power Board by the USB-C Power Cable — then the whole assembly into its holder with the lid fastened. The Potentiometer Assembly: the teacher solders the SVG wire ends to the potentiometer terminals (Figure 0.4), then the potentiometer is fastened to its holder and the gear pressed onto the shaft — a very tight fit; the manual recommends a clamp or vise.
  3. 3
    Rear electrical area — battery, fuses, switch · Stage 5
    Install the battery in the Battery Holder. Strip the ends of the two fuse holders and install them in the Level 1 Rear Wall, fastened with (4) M3x8mm. Install the power switch in the rear wall with the gold tab on the right when viewed from the back, as the manual specifies.
  4. 4
    The main electrical system — PCB, power runs, the fuse test · Stage 5
    Mount the Sourccey PCB on its holder with the buck converter, and lay the XT30 power runs — 150mm, 350mm, and the 700mm motor runs — through the lever wire connectors, labeling every run as it is laid; connect the QWIIC cable to the IMU, the thermistor, and the LED strips per the manual's routing. Then the manual's own test of the main power system, performed carefully — a wiring mistake here can spark: insert the blue 15A fuse into the top fuse holder, flip the power switch, and the switch LED must turn on; if it does not, the wiring is incorrect and gets found now. The red 10A fuse follows.
  5. 5
    Build the Teleoperator stand · Stage 1
    Fasten Teleop Stand Right to Stand Left — (2) M3x8mm. Fasten the two Motor Driver Boards to the stand — (8) M2.5x8mm — and connect their cables: the barrel-jack power cables, the Sourccey Teleop Power Cable, the wire splitter, and the two USB-C data cables into the USB splitter. Fasten an Arm Base to each side of the stand — (6) M3x20mm per side — thread a 400mm Arm Motor Cable from each driver board up through the channels to the top of its base, and close the stand with its lid — (6) M3x30mm. Orientation matters throughout this stage: parts that look symmetrical are not, and several are left/right specific.
  6. 6
    Set every motor ID, then flash the Pi OS · Stage 2
    Power the stand and connect its USB data cable to the computer. In the FD Feetech Manager software, define the COM settings — two COM ports, one per driver board — and set the baud rate to 1,000,000. Plug one servo into an arm cable, find it with Search, and write its ID in the Programming tab. Repeat for every motor, model-checked as you go: Robot Motors 1 and 7 are STS3215, 2–3 and 8–9 are STS3250, 4–6 and 10–12 are STS3215, and all twelve Teleop motors are STS3215-TELEOP. Keep track of which motor is which once its ID is set. Then flash the SD card: Raspberry Pi Imager, the latest Vulcan Pi OS as a custom image, device Raspberry Pi 5, Write.
  7. 7
    Build the two Teleoperator leader arms · Stage 3
    Per arm, in the manual's order: Motor 1 into the Arm Base; Motor 2 into the Shoulder with its support; Shoulder to Motor 1; Motor 1 Support; Forearm to Motor 2; Motors 3 and 4 into the Forearm with their shared supports; Motor 5 and its support into the Wrist — no Driven Motor Horn on Motor 5; Wrist assembly on; Motor 6 Casing with its Driven Motor Horn; Motor 6 in — no Idle Motor Horn on Motor 6; then the Handle and the Trigger. Wire each arm as it is built — 100mm and 170mm at Motor 5, then 170mm 5→6, 100mm 5→4, 200mm 4→3, 200mm 3→2, 100mm 2→1, the 400mm from the stand to Motor 1 — with every wire clip fastened as its run lands. The right arm repeats the build with its motor IDs starting at Teleop Motor 7.
  8. 8
    Check
    Every holder occupied and labeled; wiring compared run by run against the manual's routing; leader arms held side by side and mirrored.
KEY SKILLS
Cable managementElectronics careSystem thinking
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: gloves and ventilation ready for the potentiometer-wire soldering — teacher-led, per the Safety & Care page. Servo ID software ready on a classroom computer. Watch for two things: servo IDs must be set before the arms connect — an arm wired with unset IDs costs the class a disassembly later — and unlabeled cables. Every run gets its label as it is laid, not at the end.
FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
Every holder occupied and labeled; wiring follows the manual's routing; leader arms mirror each other.
Phase 1 checkpoint — before any power. Seven checkoffs passed: base, body, lift, two arms, dome, wiring. The robot is complete as a machine and has never been switched on. Phase 2 begins with software — and the first power-up is its own lesson, with its own safety checks, not a moment at the end of a build day.

Pacing Lane A · Week 9 | Lane B · Week 5 — paired with Lesson 10
GOALVerify every device, check the battery gauge, calibrate the arms and the lift, start the robot.
MU EXPLAINS IT
First power-up: you verify every device reports in, check the battery gauge, calibrate the arms and the lift, and start the robot — with the off switch located before anything moves.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    Safety restated — gauge first, off switch located by everyone before power.
  2. 2
    Power up and verify every device
    Power up, and verify every device reports in.
  3. 3
    Check the battery gauge
    Check the battery gauge before anything else, and say the reading out loud.
  4. 4
    Calibrate the arms and the lift
    Calibrate the arms and the lift, and save the calibration.

KEY SKILLS
CalibrationDiagnosticsSafety checks
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: clear floor space around the robot; chargers on hand. Watch for: a device that does not report in. Stop and diagnose — the answer is almost always a Lesson 7 cable or an unset servo ID, and finding it is the lesson, not an interruption of it.
TROUBLESHOOTING CLINIC — USE AFTER LESSON 9

First power-up is where the build tells the truth. Work this table in order — symptom, check, fix — before changing anything else. Power off before any hands-on fix, per Safety & Care.

SymptomCheckFix
A device does not report inRe-run Lesson 9's device verification, device by device, out loud, from the top.Stop and diagnose — do not carry a silent device into calibration. The answer is almost always a Lesson 7 cable or an unset servo ID.
Servo ID conflict — the wrong joint answers, or joints answer togetherCheck the servo IDs against the motor-ID programming from Lesson 7 (Stages 1–3): IDs must be set before the arms connect.Reset the conflicting ID, verify it, and only then reconnect.
A device drops out, or works only sometimesPower off, then check that run's cable: is the connector fully seated, and is the cable labeled and routed as it was laid in Lesson 7?Reseat the connector, compare the run against the manual's routing, then re-verify the device.
Battery gauge reads abnormallyRead the gauge before anything else and say the reading out loud, as at every power-up.A pack that is swollen, punctured, hot, or reading abnormally comes out of service and goes to the teacher immediately — and packs are charged only with the chargers included in the kit.

The clinic rule: stop and diagnose. A fault found here is the lesson, not an interruption of it — and no fix moves the class past a checkoff that has not passed.

FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
All devices report in; calibration saved; robot idles safely with the off switch located by every student.

GOALCapture demonstrations as episodes — e.g. the task “Fold the shirt” — keeping good takes, discarding bad ones (arrow keys save / discard).
MU EXPLAINS IT
You record demonstrations as episodes of the class task, driving the robot through it cleanly — saving the good takes and discarding the bad ones with the arrow keys.
STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL'S ORDER
  1. 1
    Open (5 min)
    The class picks its task; what a clean demonstration looks like — and what a sloppy one teaches.
  2. 2
    Record episodes of the class task
    Record episodes of the class task — the example task is “Fold the shirt.”
  3. 3
    Save the clean takes, discard the rest
    Right Arrow saves an episode; Left Arrow discards and re-records it.
  4. 4
    Check

KEY SKILLS
What makes a clean demonstrationJudging data quality
TEACHER NOTES
Prep: class task chosen and its materials ready (the example task is “Fold the shirt”). Watch for: saving every take. The discard key is the lesson — a dataset of clean episodes trains a better policy than a bigger dataset of mixed ones, and Lesson 13 will prove it.
A CLEAN EPISODE — THE BAR

An episode counts as clean only if all four hold:

  • the robot starts from a consistent start position;
  • the whole task stays in frame;
  • there are no mid-task corrections;
  • the task is carried through to a completed finish.

Anything less is discarded and re-recorded — it does not count toward the 5.

FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF
The class dataset holds at least 5 clean episodes of the class task — each one meeting the clean-episode criteria below.

Program Assessment · All 14 Lessons · Three Tracks
Evidence 14 checkoffs · the build log · the Lesson 14 presentation

Assessment rests on evidence the class produces as it goes — not on a final test. Three sources, all already in the room:

The 14 checkoffs

Every lesson's Done looks like is a checkpoint — 14 in total. Each is observable (rolls freely, calibration saved, 5 clean episodes) and signed off at the end of its lesson, while the evidence is still on the bench. A missed checkoff is fixed in the next session's open, before new work begins.

The build log

Each team keeps a build log across all 14 lessons: times, refits, decisions, training choices. The log shows process — how a team worked, what it caught, what it fixed — which the finished robot alone cannot show.

The Lesson 14 presentation

The closing presentation weighs the team's understanding: what they built, what they taught the robot, and what they would do differently. It is graded on the honesty and specificity of the account, not on a flawless final run.

TRACK DEPTH CHART — SAME ROBOT, THREE DEPTHS
Ages 10–13Ages 14–18College · 18+
BuildFull build, with guidance at the electrical and calibration stepsFull build, independently — including servo IDs, wiring, and system checksFull build, all stages
CodeFirst datasets: record, curate, and train with guidancePython + LeRobot SDK (Vulcan's lerobot-vulcan fork, Lesson 8 Path B): camera and LiDAR data, dataset management, own training runsPython + LeRobot (lerobot-vulcan) from the start
ProjectGuided team project, built from the class datasetsTeam project with own training runsOriginal research project
FinishTrained policy + team presentationTrained policy + full presentationTrained policy + research write-up

Every track builds the same robot, passes the same 14 checkoffs, and finishes with the same Lesson 14 solo performance. A younger student is not building a lesser machine — they are building the same machine with more of the room's help, and they meet the full depth when they return in an older track.

BETWEEN SESSIONS
Practise in the simulators

Sourccey has full simulators — MuJoCo and Isaac Sim — with the complete robot: arms, grippers, elevator, and mecanum drive, with interactive controls. Between sessions, students practise driving in simulation, where a mistake costs nothing and the real robot stays exactly as the last checkoff left it. Simulator time is also the answer for early finishers and snow days.

MAKER classes print one stage ahead

For MAKER classes, the print queue runs one stage ahead of the lessons: while the class builds Stage N, the printer produces Stage N+1. Parts are checked against the print queue as they come off the printer, so a failed print is discovered a week before its lesson — not during it. COMPLETE classes have no queue to run; their between-session work is the simulators and the build log.

WHAT A STUDENT WALKS AWAY WITH

A robot they built with their own hands, across 14 checked-off lessons. A dataset of their own demonstrations, and a policy they trained from it. A build log that documents all of it. And the experience the whole program is pointed at: standing in a room, hands off, watching a machine perform a task — because they taught it to.

Top fuseBlue — 15 amp
10A
Bottom fuseRed — 10 amp

Both fuses are installed and proven during the Stage 5 main-power test in the Assembly Manual — power doesn’t flow until the protection checks out.

Soldering

Lesson 7 · Teacher-led

1

Exactly ONE solder step in the whole build — the potentiometer wires in Lesson 7. Everything else is screws and connectors.

The teacher runs the iron. Students prepare, hold, and inspect.

Supervision

Every driving session

  • ✓One driver at a time — hands pass, they don’t share.
  • ✓A cleared drive area before the robot moves.
  • ✓The robot’s off switch — everyone knows where it is.
  • ✓Ages 10–13: a grown-up close by for build steps.
